stages.name: Harrod-Domar model
stages.title: Harrod-Domar model
stages.sub: How the share of income saved and the efficiency of capital together determine an economy's growth rate.

steps.q: Country A saves 5% of its national income each year, Country B saves 20%. Which country has more of its own income left over to fund new factories and equipment?
steps.hint: Saving means not spending on consumption now, so it is available for something else.

steps.q: A bank collects up savings from households and lends them out to firms building new factories. What has happened to that saved money?
steps.right: It has been turned into investment in capital
steps.wrong: It has simply disappeared from the economy
steps.hint: Savings sitting idle do nothing for growth. What has to happen to them first?

steps.q: Building a new road costs £10 million and raises the country's yearly output by £2 million. To get the same £2 million rise in output from a less efficient project, would you need to spend more or less than £10 million on capital?
steps.hint: A less efficient project needs more capital to produce the same extra output.

steps.q: Two countries save the same share of income, but Country X needs far less new capital than Country Y to produce each extra unit of output. Which country would grow faster from the same savings ratio?
steps.hint: Less capital needed per unit of extra output means each pound of investment goes further.
